status: PREDECLARED NON-CONSENSUS SECOND BOUNDED ATTACK FAMILY
question: Can a cost-aware frontier of exact historical values complete a canonical proof at half scratch memory without machine-state checkpoints or unbounded planning?

independent_strategy.base: arena-resident iterative dependency regeneration from genesis
independent_strategy.difference_from_checkpoint_policy: retain completed value pebbles by estimated regeneration cost instead of retaining machine-state bookmarks by time

frontier_policy.packed_key: stop_iteration shifted left 15 bits, bitwise-or scratch word
frontier_policy.second_candidate: first plus 1 plus ((((key xor (key shifted right 16)) * 0x85ebca6b) mod 2^32) mod 9943), modulo 9944
frontier_policy.lookup: probe both distinct candidates in order and return the first exact key match
frontier_policy.admission: update an exact key; otherwise use the first empty candidate; otherwise the second empty candidate; otherwise select the candidate with lower stop, breaking equal-stop ties toward the first candidate
frontier_policy.replacement: replace the selected resident only when the incoming stop is strictly greater; reject equal-or-lower-stop values
frontier_policy.cost_proxy: larger stop_iteration means more genesis replay and is therefore more expensive to reconstruct

charged_operations: each of two frontier candidate probes on every lookup
each of two frontier candidate probes on every admission attempt
operation_policy.invariant: total_operations equals logical_value_requests plus replay_iterations plus frontier_probes
operation_policy.failure: refuse before an operation that would exceed the ceiling and emit no proof

selected_configuration.primary_allocation: 1/128 of possible 16-byte primary slots after allocator reserve

holdout_policy.selection_rule: No parameter changes after any fixed-vector or holdout result is observed; retain all eight holdout rows, including unfavorable outcomes.

gate_mapping.reason: The new family must first establish exact independent boundaries. A gate assessment still requires canonical proofs, controlled physical-host measurements, and independent review.
